name: TRAPI
shortSummary: Transactions Repository API designed as part of monolith decomposition.
technicalDescription: TRAPI serves normalized transaction records for downstream consumers with stable contracts and operational visibility.
architecture: Harmonization layer for banking-specific payload normalization
Persistence model prepared for high-read transaction access patterns
Encrypted event publication for trusted consumers
outcomes: Supported gradual migration from legacy ETR monolith into service-based boundaries.
Improved maintainability by isolating repository concerns from legacy components.
teamNote: Developed with a backend squad. My role focused on migration tasks, API behavior discussions, and production hardening alongside teammates.

name: TRQUERY
shortSummary: Transactions Query service focused on read models and query performance.
technicalDescription: TRQUERY exposes query-oriented endpoints for transaction listing while preserving domain consistency and observability.
architecture: Read-focused API endpoints over transaction repository
Monitoring for latency and error rates
outcomes: Helped transition transaction listing responsibilities away from monolith paths.
Reduced operational friction through clearer service ownership boundaries.
teamNote: Built collaboratively inside the backend team. I contributed to query logic, integration behavior, and incident-oriented reliability work.

name: AISCAF
shortSummary: Upstream banking integration service used by external and internal consumers.
technicalDescription: AISCAF coordinates upstream data exchange under strict operational constraints and shared banking schedules.
architecture: Upstream integration with controlled deployment windows
Capacity planning with OMA and WARF responsibilities
Operational dependency handling across consumer systems
Incident response alignment with on-call practices
outcomes: Sustained stable flows for consumers such as Fintonic, BBVA, and TTPS.
Improved release confidence through coordinated night deployment routines.
teamNote: Operated by a cross-functional team. My contribution centered on operational readiness, deployment execution, and coordination across stakeholders.

name: DevOps Platform / Microservices Maintenance
shortSummary: Reliability and maintenance ownership for approximately ten production microservices.
technicalDescription: Day-to-day platform work spanning vulnerabilities, dependency updates, and incident-driven stabilization.
architecture: Security and vulnerability remediation with Checkmarx
Dependency upgrades for Spring Boot and Merak components
Metrics-driven maintenance via Grafana and Prometheus
outcomes: Maintained service stability during frequent operational changes.
Improved response readiness during 24x7 on-call rotation periods.
teamNote: This is shared platform work. I participate in planning and execution with engineers, PO, and operations; ownership is collective, not individual.

name: Swift Messaging
shortSummary: MTM Java messaging support in early banking backend phase.
technicalDescription: Handled message processing tasks and learned internal financial tooling while contributing to team delivery.
outcomes: Built familiarity with banking systems under production constraints.
Contributed to stable message handling in shared delivery cycles.
teamNote: This phase was highly collaborative. My role was supportive and execution-focused while learning domain patterns from the team.
